verdict.rationale: Adyen documents outbound webhooks sent to the merchant's server, so you don't have to poll. They cover final payment outcomes and account, merchant and store status changes, with HMAC signature verification, delivery-failure troubleshooting and event logs. The pack never documents how to register or subscribe a callback endpoint, so the reviewer's concern holds and this cannot be full. Missing for 10: documented endpoint registration/subscription (via UI or API), selection of which event types to subscribe to, POS-specific event coverage, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Webhooks solve this by sending you a message with the final outcome as soon as it is available.
With webhooks, you can avoid having to continuously poll an API endpoint, waiting for a change in status for an asynchronous process
In your Customer Area, you can find a log of all [webhook events](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks) sent to your server.
Verify the integrity of webhook events using HMAC signatures.
Account setting [webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks) inform you of status changes related to your company account, merchant accounts, and stores.
